unit.bounded_unit: PTX ISA 9.3 bounded scalar form and.b16 d, a, b;
unit.scope_boundary: Only .b16 bounded semantics for and with optional guard and two explicit register sources in this run.

compliance_notes: No proofs are written at this stage.

validation_obligations.title: Bounded syntax and operand shape
validation_obligations.description: The bounded form is and.b16 d, a, b; with optional predicate guard and operand order d, a, b.

validation_obligations.title: 16-bit bounded value representation
validation_obligations.description: B16 values are represented by Fin (2 ^ 16), enforcing the bounded width invariant in type.

validation_obligations.title: Minimal state and partial outcome shape
validation_obligations.description: Machine state includes register and predicate maps only; execAndB16 is partial via Option.none for malformed reads or missing guard predicate.

theorem_obligations.intent: For fixed pre-state and instruction, the one-step relation has at most one result state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For all states s, instructions i, and states s1, s2: if AndB16Step s i s1 and AndB16Step s i s2 then s1 = s2.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem AndB16Step_deterministic (s : MachineState) (i : AndB16Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState) (h1 : AndB16Step s i s1) (h2 : AndB16Step s i s2) : s1 = s2
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Both constructors (executed, guardFalse) are possible in the bounded definition, so uniqueness is a substantive relational property, not a function-application tautology.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case split on h1 and h2. Constructor mismatch is impossible by contradictory guard results. Same-constructor cases reduce to equal update expressions (executed case) or reflexivity (guardFalse).

theorem_obligations.intent: Relate execAndB16 outcomes to AndB16Step in both directions and characterize none exactly as no possible step.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If execAndB16 returns executed or guardFalse, then the corresponding AndB16Step holds; if a step holds then execAndB16 returns a matching outcome. Also, execAndB16 returns none iff no AndB16Step exists for that state and instruction.
hypotheses: h : execAndB16 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')
h : execAndB16 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Function/relation outcomes are equivalent up to constructor cases, and none occurs iff no step exists.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: execAndB16 includes both executed/guardFalse branches and none; the theorem does substantive case analysis across all branches.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execAndB16 and AndB16Step; prove each direction by constructor/branch split over guard and source lookups.

theorem_obligations.intent: If guard is true and both source lookups resolve in the pre-state, then destination write is exactly a bitwise AND of source values.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: Given guard-true, explicit register destination r, and source values va/vb from evalSourceA and evalSourceB, execAndB16 returns an executed state in which r contains andValue va vb.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem execAndB16_and_result (s : MachineState) (i : AndB16Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B16) (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) (ha : evalSourceA s i.a = some va) (hb : evalSourceB s i.b = some vb) :
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : evalSourceA s i.a = some va
hb : evalSourceB s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Exists s', execAndB16 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') and s'.valueRegs r = some (andValue va vb)
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: This ties the post-state value to the explicit semantics text d = a & b, not just to generic state change.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Use hguard and source hypotheses to force the executed branch of execAndB16 and simplify updateDestination under hd.

theorem_obligations.intent: When the guard predicate is false, no modeled state changes occur.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any guard-false AndB16Step from s, the result state is s.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem AndB16Step_false_guard_preserves_state (s : MachineState) (i : AndB16Instruction) (h : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) (hstep : AndB16Step s i s) : s = s
hypotheses: h : evalGuard s i.guard = some false
theorem_obligations.conclusion: State is unchanged under false guard.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: This validates the explicit `@` no-op branch by checking the relation constructor semantics directly.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: In this bounded model, the false-guard constructor returns the same pre-state; rewrite by constructor and close by reflexivity.

theorem_obligations.intent: Executed steps only update value registers and preserve predicate registers in the bounded model.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For an AndB16Step relation with register destination, every predicate register p has unchanged value across source and target states.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem AndB16Step_predicates_preserved (s : MachineState) (i : AndB16Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (r : RegId) (h : AndB16Step s i s') (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) : forall p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Predicates are preserved by any one-step execution.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The predicate file is part of the state model, so checking its invariance is a meaningful frame property given the bounded semantics.
